text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Deputy Prime Minister Tansu Ciller asks Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan to hand over the premiership and work for early elections.
- Erbakan's government will begin selling off state-owned coastal camps as time-share resorts in June.
MILLIYET
- Senior conservative deputy Necmettin Cevheri calls on Ciller to pull out of the coalition in order to avoid damaging their True Path Party.
- Turkish armed forces staff were briefed by leading trade unionist and trade ministry officials on the economy, privatisation, unions and social security.
HURRIYET
- President Suleyman Demirel says foreign countries do not have a true understanding of Turkey's secular image.
- Thirty-six out of 100 bathrobes imported by the United States are made in Turkey.
YENI YUZYIL
- The cabinet had an eventful meeting after a seven-week break, with Ciller warning Erbakan that the military will shut his Welfare Party down if he does not call early elections.
- Conservative Defence Minister Turhan Tayan did not attend the cabinet meeting on Tuesday amid rumours that he is on the brink of resigning.
RADIKAL
- The Turkish trade deficit for 1996 has been announced as $19.4 billion. In this period importats grew by 32.5 percent whereas exports grew by only 3.7 percent.
DUNYA

- Turkey's plans to import Kazakh and Turkmen natural gas and oil will suffer drawbacks because Islamist Taleban forces have taken over the whole of Afghanistan, paving the way for new pipeline routes through Taleban ally Pakistan. The original plans had been to take the pipelines through Turkey.
- A commission debating raising the minimum wage has begun talks.
ZAMAN
- Erbakan tells his party MPs that he had to give his approval to the sacking of 161 Islamists from the military or be forced to withdraw from the government.
CUMHURIYET

- The military-dominated National Security Council (MGK) is reported to be working on new "precautions package" that would help the implementation of its demands, made in February, that the government crack down on Islamist zeal.
